entities.description: The root of the powers of Fire. A great flaming torch or club, blazing with divine creative energy. In the Thoth system, this represents the pure Yod of Atziluth — the fiery creative impulse at its most primal.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Creative force, primal energy, will, spiritual fire, new enterprise, courage
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Blocked will, creative drought, sterile ambition, false starts

entities.description: Dominion. Mars in Aries — the fiercest manifestation of fire. Two crossed wands in the form of a cross over a rose cross background. Represents raw power, authority, and the will to dominate through force of personality.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Dominion, authority, power, boldness, will, command, direct action
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Domineering, abuse of power, hastiness, ruthlessness

entities.description: Virtue. Sun in Aries — the natural beneficence of fire. Three wands arranged like a trident with lotus heads. Represents established strength, completed effort, virtue, and the confident expression of creative will.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Virtue, confidence, established strength, leadership, creative expression, foresight
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Arrogance, pomposity, vain confidence, squandered strength

entities.description: Completion. Venus in Aries — beauty and harmony arising from fire. Four wands topped with rams' heads and doves. Represents completion, settlement, and the harmonious completion of a creative work.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Completion, settlement, social success, beauty, harmony, perfected work
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Unreliability, inconstancy, wavering, lack of completion

entities.description: Strife. Saturn in Leo — the destructive limitation of fire's proud expression. Five wands in conflict. Represents violent struggle, quarrel, and the disruption of established order through competitive strife.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Strife, violent struggle, competition, contest, boldness in conflict
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Litigation, quarrels, cruelty, vexation, destructive conflict

entities.description: Victory. Jupiter in Leo — the triumphant expansion of fire. Six wands forming a nexus pattern. Represents victory gained through noble effort, fulfillment of desire, and the expression of pride in achievement.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Victory, pride, nobility, love, conceit satisfied, desire fulfilled
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Pride leading to fall, arrogance, unstable success

entities.description: Valour. Mars in Leo — courage under fire. Seven wands in conflict, with one prominent wand holding the center. Represents courage and the ability to maintain one's ground against overwhelming opposition.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Valour, courage, holding firm, opposition met with bravery, possible victory
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Indecision, wavering, embarrassment, danger from enemies

entities.description: Swiftness. Mercury in Sagittarius — the swift communicative arrow of fire. Eight wands arranged as light rays. Represents swift movement, rapid communication, and the rapid resolution of matters through decisive action.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Swiftness, speed, rapidity, hasty communications, too-swift action, electric energy

entities.description: Strength. Moon in Sagittarius — the reflective, gathered strength of fire. Nine wands in a balanced arrangement. Represents the recovery and gathering of strength, great force in reserve, and powerful defensive capability.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Strength, recovery, great force, health, success in completion, power held in reserve

entities.description: Oppression. Saturn in Sagittarius — the crushing limitation of fire's expansive nature. Ten wands arranged as crossed clubs in a heavy, burdensome pattern. Represents cruel and overbearing force, exhausted strength, and oppressive power.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Oppression, cruelty, malice, overbearing force, injustice, falsity
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Cunning, deceiving, unkindness — oppression turned inward

entities.description: The earthly manifestation of fire's creative force. The Princess (equivalent to RWS Page) stands energetically, holding a wand with a tiger at her feet. Represents brilliance, courage, beauty, and sudden creative force that can be destructive if undisciplined.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Brilliance, courage, beauty, force, sudden energy, enthusiasm, the earth of fire

entities.description: The airy aspect of fire — swift and fiery in action. The Prince (equivalent to RWS Knight) rides a chariot drawn by a lion. Represents swift, violent, and impulsive action; passionate energy that can be constructive or destructive.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Swift energy, fiery action, generosity, arrogance in nobility, the air of fire

entities.description: The watery aspect of fire — adaptable, nurturing fire. The Queen sits on a throne holding a wand topped with a pine cone, a leopard at her side. Represents adaptable and steady fire, command, beauty, and fierce protectiveness.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Adaptability, persistent energy, command, will, authority, the water of fire

entities.description: The fiery aspect of fire — the purest, most concentrated fire. The Knight (equivalent to RWS King) charges on a flaming horse. Represents pure, active, volatile fire energy; swift, fierce, and noble, yet potentially rash and destructive.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Fire of fire, pure will, swiftness, activity, generosity, fierceness, the true king of fire
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Cruel, intolerant, violent, rash decisions, fanatical

entities.description: The root of the powers of Water. A great lotus cup overflowing with radiant streams. Represents pure emotional and spiritual potential, the divine feminine in its fullness, and the unconditioned love at the heart of existence.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Fertility, productiveness, beauty, pleasure, happiness, spiritual love

entities.description: Love. Venus in Cancer — the beauty and tenderness of emotional union. Two cups with a lotus between them. Represents love, harmony, and the pleasure of two hearts in perfect accord.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Love, harmony, pleasure, warmth, tenderness, friendship, emotional union
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Folly, waste, cross purposes, misunderstood love

entities.description: Abundance. Mercury in Cancer — the communicative joy of emotional plenty. Three cups overflowing into each other. Represents abundance, pleasure, and the celebration of emotional richness shared with others.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Abundance, joy, plenty, pleasure, hospitality, healing, celebration
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Excess, overindulgence, dissolution, sensuality gone wrong

entities.description: Luxury. Moon in Cancer — the surfeit of emotional comfort. Four cups in a stable arrangement with lotus flowers. Represents the excess of pleasure that leads to dissatisfaction, the boredom of too much comfort.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Luxury, mixed pleasure, apprehension, blended delight and unease

entities.description: Disappointment. Mars in Scorpio — the violent disruption of emotional peace. Five cups in troubled arrangement. Represents disappointment, sorrow, and the emotional suffering that comes when expectations are not met.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Disappointment, sorrow, unkindness, treachery, bitter news
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Vain regret, idle sorrow, crying over spilt milk

entities.description: Pleasure. Sun in Scorpio — the transformative warmth of deep emotional pleasure. Six cups in harmonious arrangement overflowing. Represents beauty, harmony in pleasure, and the past returning in a positive way.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Pleasure, harmony, beauty, delight, enjoyment, wish fulfillment
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Past stagnation, wishful thinking, imperfect pleasure

entities.description: Debauch. Venus in Scorpio — the perversion of pleasure into excess and corruption. Seven cups in a deteriorated arrangement, many leaking or spilling. Represents debauchery, corruption of desire, and the dissolution of the will through indulgence.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Debauch, corruption, illusory success, deceit, promises unfulfilled
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Slight tendency toward evil — still passive corruption

entities.description: Indolence. Saturn in Pisces — the inertia and depression of still waters. Eight cups in a tired, drooping arrangement. Represents indolence, abandonment of effort, and the disappointment that comes from failed enterprise.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Indolence, abandoned success, misery, disappointment, giving up
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Instability, lack of persistence, wasted effort

entities.description: Happiness. Jupiter in Pisces — the expansive joy of spiritual water. Nine cups in a balanced, overflowing arrangement. Represents complete happiness, satisfaction in material and emotional realms.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Complete success, wish fulfilled, happiness, physical well-being, plenty
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Overconfidence, material gain at spiritual expense

entities.description: Satiety. Mars in Pisces — the disruption of perfect contentment by aggression. Ten cups overflowing but with an unsettled quality. Represents satiety, surfeit, and the completion that paradoxically brings a new unrest.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Satiety, gluttony, culmination of wish, peace, and then — the problem of too much

entities.description: The earthy aspect of water — dreams made tangible. The Princess stands by water holding a crystal cup. Represents gentle and loving nature, psychic gifts, romantic dreams, and the beautiful imagination of deep waters.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Gentle, kind, tender, imaginative, psychic, the earth of water

entities.description: The airy aspect of water — intellectual emotion, sublimated feeling. The Prince in a chariot drawn by an eagle. Represents the subtle, crafty personality driven by desire beneath an exterior of calm; secretly intense.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Subtlety, secret power, artistic sensitivity, the air of water, inner intensity
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Ruthless, violent, crafty for evil ends

entities.description: The watery aspect of water — pure psychic power and emotional intelligence. The Queen sits on a throne with water imagery, crayfish and shells at her feet. Represents imagination, dream, and psychic perception at its deepest.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Psychic, imaginative, reflective, poetic, tranquil, the water of water
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Selfish, vain, unstable, possible vice, dishonesty

entities.description: The fiery aspect of water — passionate feeling, the ardor of the deep. The Knight rides a white horse over water. Represents the sublimated passion and the beauty of emotional depth in motion.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Grace, poetry, beauty in action, romance, the fire of water
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Idle, untruthful, acting from selfish emotion

entities.description: The root of the powers of Air. A great upright sword crowned with a divine crown, emanating light. Represents the pure intellect as a double-edged force — capable of truth and destruction in equal measure.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Invoked or Evoked force, a double-edged sword, triumph of mind, clarity

entities.description: Peace. Moon in Libra — the rational balance achieved through equal opposing forces. Two swords crossed. Represents a temporary truce, the peace of a balanced mind, and intellectual equilibrium.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Peace, balanced power, equipoise, restored peace, yet uneasy calm
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Indecision, confusion, inability to make peace last

entities.description: Sorrow. Saturn in Libra — the weight of cold logic inflicting grief. Three swords piercing a rose. Represents unhappy love, deep sorrow, and the pain of clear-eyed reality severing illusion.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Sorrow, unhappy love, strife, disruption, tears, separation

entities.description: Truce. Jupiter in Libra — a temporary but stable ceasefire. Four swords in a cross arrangement. Represents a retreat to gather strength, a necessary pause, and the establishment of peace through treaty.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Truce, rest, recuperation, retreat, armed peace, temporary respite

entities.description: Defeat. Venus in Aquarius — the beauty of idealism crushed by practical defeat. Five swords in disarray. Represents defeat, surrender, and the sometimes necessary acknowledgment that a battle is lost.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Defeat, loss, failure, dishonor, malice, treachery

entities.description: Science. Mercury in Aquarius — the precision of intellect applied to universal truth. Six swords in a perfectly balanced geometric arrangement. Represents earning success through the careful application of intelligence and method.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Science, earned success, beauty, skill, intelligence applied, systematic effort

entities.description: Futility. Moon in Aquarius — the dreamlike detachment undermining the sword's purpose. Seven swords in an unstable arrangement. Represents unstable effort, partial success, and the futility of action without commitment.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Futility, unsteadiness, partial success, journey, evasion

entities.description: Interference. Jupiter in Gemini — the scattered, interfering energy that disrupts clear thinking. Eight swords in a chaotic pattern. Represents narrow, restricted action, and the petty mind that interferes with larger progress.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Interference, restriction, petty restrictions, narrowness, bickering

entities.description: Cruelty. Mars in Gemini — the violent lacerating force of destructive thought. Nine swords dripping blood. Represents despair, cruelty, and the mental torment of destructive thought patterns.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Despair, cruelty, pitilessness, malice, suffering, illness of mind

entities.description: Ruin. Sun in Gemini — the final dissolution of intellect when used against itself. Ten swords in total destruction. Represents complete ruin, the final destruction of a way of thinking, and the ultimate defeat of the mind by its own devices.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Ruin, disruption, death, defeat, undeniable end, catastrophic loss

entities.description: The earthy aspect of air — thought made concrete. The Princess stands in a stormy landscape with a sword raised. Represents a keen, even cutting intellect applied to earthly matters; a skillful logician and debater.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Keen observation, logic, the earth of air, decisive minor action

entities.description: The airy aspect of air — pure intellectual power in motion. The Prince charges on a winged chariot. Represents skill in language and ideas, but a tendency to be all intellect with no feeling.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Skill, the air of air, diligence, swift intellect, cleverness

entities.description: The watery aspect of air — perception and feeling blended with sharp intellect. The Queen holds a severed head in one hand. Represents keen perception, grief transmuted into clear-eyed wisdom, and truth without sentiment.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Perceptive, subtle, keen intellect, the water of air, sorrow experienced and transcended

entities.description: The fiery aspect of air — the most active and volatile of all air energies. The Knight rides a galloping horse. Represents intense, purposeful intellect; the capacity for great good or great harm through the power of the mind.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Fierce, subtle, clever, the fire of air, great power of mind, strong will

entities.description: The root of the powers of Earth. A great golden disk marked with a complex mandala. Represents the material world's pure creative potential, solid manifestation, and the ground of all physical existence.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Material gain, prosperity, wealth, contentment, the root of earth's power
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Prosperity without satisfaction, false material success

entities.description: Change. Jupiter in Capricorn — expansive change in earth matters. Two disks joined by an infinity symbol. Represents harmonious change, pleasant alternation, and the natural fluctuation of material fortune.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Change, harmonious fluctuation, juggling resources, pleasant change

entities.description: Works. Mars in Capricorn — applied energy producing tangible results. Three disks in a triangular arrangement. Represents skilled labor, construction, and the pride of work accomplished through focused effort.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Work, building, skilled construction, commercial success, creativity applied

entities.description: Power. Sun in Capricorn — the solidity and stability of earthly power. Four disks in a castle-like arrangement. Represents law and order, earthly power well established, and the material security that comes from discipline.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Power, earthly power, law and order, material security, rigid establishment

entities.description: Worry. Mercury in Taurus — the restless mind disrupting material stability. Five disks in an inverted pentagram arrangement. Represents material loss, anxiety, and the mental suffering caused by financial insecurity.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Worry, material trouble, poverty, anxiety, loss, ruin, squalor
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Chaos, disorder, greed leading to ruin

entities.description: Success. Moon in Taurus — the fruitful, abundant earth in its most stable expression. Six disks in a perfect hexagonal arrangement. Represents material success, generosity in prosperity, and the just reward of effort.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Success, material gain, prosperity, generosity, present success

entities.description: Failure. Saturn in Taurus — the contraction and limitation of earth's bounty. Seven disks in a heavy, downward-pressing arrangement. Represents unproductive labor, failure despite effort, and the frustration of unrewarded work.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Failure, unprofitable work, blight, unrewarded effort, hoping against hope
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Anxiety, little gain for much effort

entities.description: Prudence. Sun in Virgo — the careful, analytical application of practical skill. Eight disks in a careful arrangement. Represents skill in craft, careful work, and the intelligent application of practical knowledge.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Prudence, skill, craft, diligence in practice, intelligent mastery

entities.description: Gain. Venus in Virgo — the beauty of material abundance refined. Nine disks in a satisfying arrangement. Represents material gain, accomplishment, and the prosperity that comes from skill and virtue.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Material gain, wisdom applied, prosperity, favorable enterprise, skill rewarded
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Vain worry about material things, deceit

entities.description: Wealth. Mercury in Virgo — communication and intelligence completing the material world. Ten disks arranged in the Tree of Life pattern. Represents complete material wealth, inheritance, and the fullest possible earthly success.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Wealth, inheritance, prosperity, riches, material success complete

entities.description: The earthy aspect of earth — the most material of all court cards. The Princess stands in a grove, holding a disk carved with a flower. Represents pragmatic, generous, and diligent earth; the thoughtful student of material wisdom.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Generous, diligent, benevolent, the earth of earth, material wisdom
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Wasteful, prodigal, indolent, luxurious without sense

entities.description: The airy aspect of earth — methodical intelligence applied to earthly matters. The Prince drives a chariot pulled by a bull. Represents patient, laborious, and careful activity; the engineer and master craftsman.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Methodical, patient, laborious, reliable, the air of earth, careful manager
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Animal, brutal, dull, enslaved to matter

entities.description: The watery aspect of earth — the receptive and nurturing earth. The Queen sits on a throne in a fruitful landscape. Represents the mothering, nurturing force of the earth; sensual, practical, and deeply generous.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Nuturing, sensual, practical, generous, the water of earth, domestic wisdom
extendedData.reversedMeaning: Dull, servile, foolish, possibly a trustworthy person gone wrong

entities.description: The fiery aspect of earth — the most stubborn and hardworking of all knights. The Knight sits on a heavy draft horse, holding a disk. Represents slow, methodical, but invincible material force; the farmer king.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Laborious, patient, heavy, material mastery, the fire of earth, reliable provider
